title: Abnormal chromosome 5 — terminal p-arm deletion
clinical_history: Identify pter, p, centromere, q, and qter on this abnormal chromosome 5, then assemble or compare the map. Distal short-arm material is missing (cri-du-chat). Demonstration segments; not a clinical specimen.
hints: The short-arm telomeric segments of chromosome 5 are missing from the piece set.
A terminal p-arm deletion shortens p without changing chromosome count.
ISCN writes del(5)(p15.2) after the sex-chromosome complement.
anatomy_hints: Compare short-arm length on the two maps. pter is still the top of the remaining p arm.
The change is confined to one arm. Name the class of rearrangement and the distal p-arm band where the maps diverge.
explanation: The abnormal chromosome is produced by deleting distal 5p segments from the normal ordered map. The remaining segments still run pter→cen→qter, but pter now begins at a more proximal p-arm band. That transformation corresponds to del(5)(p15.2) and, constitutionally, cri-du-chat syndrome.
plain_language_interpretation: Chromosome 5 with a terminal deletion of 5p involving band p15.
